The global market could face a diesel shortage as early as the second quarter of 2027, Reuters reports. Despite a 24% drop in diesel futures prices in November, the effects of the war with Iran, launched by Trump, continue to weigh on the fuel market. Diesel exports from the Middle East remain at just one-third of their pre-war levels. Meanwhile, Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries have cut Russia’s diesel exports fourfold, from 800,000 to 200,000 barrels per day. In 2025, Russia and the Middle East together accounted for more than 28% of global diesel exports. The situation could worsen due to extensive scheduled maintenance at oil refineries in 2027. European diesel inventories are already 19% below their level a year ago, while US stockpiles recently fell to their lowest point since 2003. Although the International Energy Agency (IEA) currently forecasts a slight surplus, analysts at Kpler expect diesel prices to remain elevated at least until mid-2027. As a result, even a further drop in crude oil prices may not translate into cheaper diesel. Persistently high fuel costs could fuel inflation by increasing expenses for freight transport and agricultural production, ultimately pushing up food prices.
